A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ACE estimation study. Their main text, equations, three figures, and Appendices A–I support comparison without material gaps.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix H report original synthetic demand-estimation experiments, including estimation errors, confidence-interval coverage, and sensitivity to dependence and sparsity.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix H retain these original simulation results, including estimator comparisons and robustness analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same sample splitting, empirical cumulant construction, moment functions, and estimating equation. The expanded sparse-regression analysis concerns the existing ACE procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic demand-estimation setting and the same covariate-dependent treatment-noise scenario. The expanded sparse-linear-regression corollary is theoretical, not additional experimental coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains ACE orders 1, 2, 3, and 5; Figures 2–3 retain orders 1, 2, and 5. The identification of first-order ACE with DML and the relationship to Mackey et al.'s estimators remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The simulation distributions, Lasso nuisance estimation, metrics, and sample-size and sparsity sweeps are unchanged. Appendix H retains n=20000 and dimension 100 for the dependence experiment, and n=10000 and dimension 1000 for the sparsity experiment; changing the dimension symbol to p is not a setting change.

E4.justification: Appendix H retains the same analyses of estimator order, sample size, covariate–noise dependence, and sparsity. Figures 2–3 provide the same sensitivity curves and estimator distributions.

E5.justification: Figure 1 still specifies 20000 independent replicates and 95% confidence bands. The plug-in interval construction and distributional displays are unchanged; the new checklist merely reiterates the existing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figures 1–3 and their reported empirical findings are unchanged. For example, Figure 1d/e retains RMSE values of 0.0747 for first-order ACE and 0.0503 for fifth-order ACE, while Appendix H retains the reported deterioration under stronger covariate–noise dependence.

T1.justification: v1's Corollary G.2 establishes a third-order Lasso specialization with s=o(n^(3/4)/log p). v3's Corollary G.3 extends this to general order r and separate nuisance sparsities, requiring max(s1, s1^(r/(r+1))s2^(1/(r+1)))=o(n^(r/(r+1))/log p), with an explicit probability bound and expanded proof. This extends an existing specialization; the central lower bounds and general ACE theorems remain unchanged. Lemma 5.1's proof is relocated, not newly added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: DML optimality for Gaussian and binary treatments, higher-order ACE robustness under independent non-Gaussian noise, and practical benefits demonstrated through synthetic demand estimation.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 now explicitly interprets general-order ACE through weaker sparsity requirements than DML. Appendix G/H qualifies the earlier blanket description of super-exponential constants by noting that cumulant growth can offset them, referring to the retained Remark 5.4. The independence limitation and empirical failure conditions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The new checklist states that open-source code is supplied in supplementary materials and that the experiments can run on a laptop. Both versions already provide the same GitHub access information. No precise new hardware specifications, runtimes, or experimental hyperparameters are supplied.

R1.justification: v3 adds Hastie, Tibshirani, and Wainwright (2015) and makes the sparsity comparison with Chernozhukov et al. (2018) more explicit. It removes the brief Section 5.1 comparison with Wang et al. (2008), while retaining that reference and its substantive treatment in Appendix I.

P1.justification: v3 trims several explanatory passages, moves Lemma 5.1's proof to Appendix G.1, reorganizes the sparse-regression material, and adds a NeurIPS checklist and conference footer. It also removes the internal comment 'LM: what is E?'. Most wording and the overall scientific narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The three figures retain their panels, axes, legends, and plotted content. Limited presentation changes include the Figure 1f caption wording, reflowed theorem and algorithm placement, an inline variance formula, and layout changes accompanying the checklist and reorganized appendix.

improvement.justification: The general-order sparse-regression corollary and fuller proof in v3's Appendix G.5 broaden and clarify an application previously stated only for third-order ACE. The explicit DML comparison and removal of an internal drafting comment also help. These are limited gains: the central theory, method, and empirical evidence remain essentially unchanged, and some explanatory intuition is shortened.
